'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[Marco Rubio]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Marco Rubio]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Marco Rubio series}}{{Elections in Florida}} The '''2022 United States Senate election in Florida''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Florida]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party of Florida|Republican]] Senator [[Marco Rubio]] won re-election to a third term, defeating [[Florida Democratic Party|Democratic]] nominee [[Val Demings]] in a [[landslide victory]]. Rubio was first elected in [[2010 United States Senate election in Florida|2010]], filling the seat of appointed Senator [[George LeMieux]]. Rubio won re-election to a third term, becoming the first Republican to do so in Florida history.{{Cite news |date=2022-11-08 |title=Florida Governor Election Results |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2022/11/08/us/elections/results-florida-governor.html |access-date=2022-11-09 |issn=0362-4331}} Rubio was sworn in for what would be his last term in the Senate, serving from January 3, 2023, to January 21, 2025, when he assumed the office of [[United States Secretary of State]] in the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second Trump administration]]. The primary elections for Republicans and Democrats took place on August 23 to finalize candidates for the November election.{{Cite web |title=United States Senate election in Florida, 2022 |url=https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Florida,_2022 |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Election Dates - Division of Elections - Florida Department of State |url=https://dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates/ |access-date=2022-06-28 |website=dos.myflorida.com}} Rubio won the uncontested Republican primary, while incumbent [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Val Demings]] won the Democratic nomination. Despite some predicting a close race early,{{cite web | url=https://www.bet.com/article/94yw4b/val-demings-slightly-behind-marco-rubio-florida-election-poll | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221103173849/https://www.bet.com/article/94yw4b/val-demings-slightly-behind-marco-rubio-florida-election-poll | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 3, 2022 | title=Val Demings Could be Victorious in Florida Senate Race, Poll Suggests | website=[[BET]] }} Rubio went on to win by a comfortable 16.4%, improving upon his [[2016 United States Senate election in Florida|2016]] performance by 8.7%. According to exit polls, Rubio won 64% of White voters, 56% of Latino voters, and 9% of African American voters (down from 17% from 2016).{{cite news |title=Florida Senatorial exit poll |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2022/exit-polls/florida/senate/0 |access-date=December 24, 2022 |publisher=[[CNN]]}} Demings' 41.27% share of the vote was the worst performance for a Democrat in a Senate race in Florida since [[1994 United States Senate election in Florida|1994]].
